Triage (seat `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr` — urgent direct triage): lands in `domain:services` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`) · p1 · Bug · `area:access`; rationale: the delegated-admin gate looks up an organization-scoped anchor by name under a context that carries no organization, so in a walled posture another tenant's business-unit tree can answer this tenant's delegation check

`Path: 真挡得住的权限 | identity-auth.invitation-scope-gates (P1, state ②) | P② | p1`
Graded at 2026-09-23T03:12Z.

**p1, not p0.** NORTH-STAR 优先级 rule 1 grades a security boundary ahead of the path, so the grade does not fall to where the path alone would put it. It stops short of p0 because the tenant wall still holds below the gate. The card measured that no org B row is read or written: update and delete fail the pre-image RLS re-read, and an org B insert fails the Layer 0 forge guard. What gets through is org B's business-unit ids in the caller's delegable-scope read, an assignment row in the caller's own org that carries an org B `business_unit_id`, and a delegate denied inside its own subtree. The p0s in this class crossed the wall itself (#15256 read and wrote another org's rows). The nearest sibling, #14946 (approvals resolving business-unit members with no org predicate), was p1. Checklist: `identity-auth.invitation-scope-gates` (P1) already treats a delegable-scope report naming a BU subtree the caller cannot delegate as a FAIL, but none of its steps boots two organizations that share a unit name. That is state ②: the fix round adds the step, and the grade inherits P1.

**Verified at source on `origin/main` `041c8cf62b`.** Only the premises were checked; the probe was not re-run, and the measurement is the filer's.

| premise | at the line |
|:--|:--|
| the gate's context carries no organization | `delegated-admin-gate.ts:44` `const SYSTEM_CTX = { isSystem: true } as const;` |
| the anchor is found by name only, `limit: 1` | `:912` `ql.find('sys_business_unit', { where: { name: businessUnitName }, limit: 1, context: SYSTEM_CTX })`; the descendant walk at `:933-937` uses the same context and has no org predicate |
| `ql` is the raw engine | `security-plugin.ts:1469-1473` builds the gate with the `objectql` service (`:1212`) |
| the engine passes a tenant only when the context has one | `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:4295` `hasTenant = execCtx?.tenantId !== undefined && …`; `:4316` sets `opts.tenantId` only under it |
| the driver scopes nothing without one | `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:13777` `applyTenantScope` returns early when `tenantId` is undefined, null or empty |
| both middlewares let a system context through | `security-plugin.ts:1782`; `packages/plugins/organizations/src/organizations-plugin.ts:308` |
| `sys_business_unit.name` is not unique | `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-business-unit.object.ts:99-105` declares no uniqueness; the only unique index is `:262`, `['code', 'organization_id']` |
| the posture is supported | ADR-0132: 「single-database organization isolation ships open」 |

The repair precedent is also on `main`: `security-plugin.ts:1348-1356` passes the caller's organization into the same kind of by-name read, so the read goes through `applyTenantScope`. That is a lead for the round, ⛔ not a prescription.

**More reads for the round in the same file, by the same mechanism.** Read at the line only; ⛔ their reach is not measured. `sys_position.name` is unique per organization (`sys-position.object.ts:357`), and the gate reads it by name under the same context at `:586` (`positionIsDelegatable`) and `:1005` (`setsBoundToPosition`). The tenant-admin branch of `describeDelegableScope` lists `sys_position` (`:338`) and `sys_business_unit` (`:351`) with no org predicate at all. The round measures each one before its diff covers it, and names any it leaves.

Dedupe, this act: two issue searches and one PR search. No open card or PR names `delegated-admin-gate.ts` or `resolveSubtree`. #14946 and #10153 are closed precedents. #19461 is the same gate but a different defect (the blank anchor, `needs-user-decision`), so ⛔ not a duplicate.

Type: `Bug`, carried by the `bug` label. The native issue type is not set, because its only channel is MCP `issue_write`, which lock 1 denies.

## Review — ACCEPT; CI converging; and ⚠️ a measured class-(a) sibling defect that this seat CANNOT file today

`Reviewed-by:` `domain:services` PM seat · `session_01AhQASwqJr2Z7XfGWUdvnbF` · 2026-09-23T06:09Z
`Implemented-by:` PR #19800 @ `da621549c0`

Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report's self-narrative.

### The claim most worth checking, checked at the source

The report says the two public methods take the caller context as a new OPTIONAL argument and that the interface **already declared it**. A new optional parameter on a published method would otherwise be a contract widening, so I read the contract source rather than the report — and rather than the CHANGELOG, which only quotes it. `origin/main`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts:714`:

```ts
describeDelegableScope(callerContext?: SecurityContext): Promise<DelegableScope>;
```

⇒ the parameter was already in the published contract; the implementation simply never used it. That is `SKILL.md:525` 「拉回已声明契约不触它」, not a widening. `Clause-②: no` stands as declared.

### Verified, each by its own read

- **Shape / scope.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #19775`, one closing hit. 5 files: the gate, the plugin, two test files, one changeset. **`packages/spec` touched: 0.** ⛔ No `content/docs/releases/**`.
- **No new module-scope export.** Diffed `^export` lines before vs after on BOTH touched sources: **IDENTICAL** each. ⇒ the mechanical floor (`contract-review.md:12`) is not tripped.
- **Fail-closed, visible in the diff rather than asserted.** `SYSTEM_CTX` gives way to `organizationScopedCtx(organizationId)` on the anchor read, the descendant walk and the catalog reads; `callerOrganizationId` resolves `organizationId ?? tenantId` — the same spelling permission sets already resolve with; and `!organizationId || rowOrganizationId(r) === organizationId` keeps the organization-less `single` posture working, pinned. The root cause is written down where the next reader will hit it: `sys_business_unit.name` carries **no** uniqueness.
- **The before/after exercises the crossing itself**, which is the only evidence that counts here: the BEFORE run reports the org-A delegate both **losing its own subtree** and **the gate APPROVING a write anchored in org B**, with ids ordered so the other organization's rows sort first; AFTER, 8/8. A test that passed on both sides would have proved nothing.
- **⛔ No existing test asserted the defect**, so nothing was "fixed" by widening an admission decision — the line I put in the dispatch word as the thing most likely to go wrong. It did not.

### Hold — CI has not converged

At `da621549c0`: 12 success, 3 skipped, **16 `in_progress`**, **zero failures**. Honest draft-time reading, ⛔ not a rework reason. ⛔ Not ready, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ not enqueued.

### ⚠️ Class (a), measured by me on this branch, and NOT fixed here

The dev reported it and correctly did not fix it. I verified it rather than relaying it. On the PR branch, in the **same file**, the same defect class survives on two **authority** decisions:

| site (on the branch) | call |
|:--|:--|
| `delegated-admin-gate.ts:661` — `positionIsDelegatable` | `ql.find('sys_position', { where: { name: positionName }, limit: 1, context: SYSTEM_CTX })` |
| `delegated-admin-gate.ts:1130` — `setsBoundToPosition` | same shape, same bare `SYSTEM_CTX` |

The bulk `sys_position` read in the same file **was** scoped by this PR (`:402`), so the contrast is inside one file. `sys_position` is a per-organization catalog row upserted by `(name, organization_id)`, so two organizations may hold a position of the same name and the driver's id ordering decides which answers — deciding whether a position may be SELF-DELEGATED (ADR-0091 D3 rule 5) and which permission sets a position distributes.

⇒ **A card is owed.** ⛔ Not folded here: each site needs its own two-organization fixture and witness, which is a verification surface this card does not carry, and the ruling-shaped rule against widening a PR applies.

⚠️ **This seat cannot file it in this fire, and that is a limitation, not a judgement.** `references/filing-gate.md` on `origin/main`: 「用户类写绑作者…一个 fire 的首写回读 `user.type`。读到 `User` ⇒ 记座位贴、本 fire ⛔ 不立新卡」. This seat's writes read back `user.type: User`, and there is no `claude[bot]` write surface in this container. So the finding is recorded HERE, in full, with its dedupe words, so that nothing is lost while the card is owed:

`delegated-admin-gate sys_position by-name read cross-org` · `positionIsDelegatable setsBoundToPosition SYSTEM_CTX no organization predicate` · `sys_position name not unique limit 1 delegatable`

Recorded as the boundary of the repair, ⛔ NOT as a defect: `businessUnitsOfUser` and `assignmentAnchorsOfPosition` read under the same bare context but are keyed on a globally unique id, so the name-collision class does not reach them.

### Landing to-do

On green: ready → auto-merge only after `mergeable_state` settles to a stable `clean` (⛔ not after a fixed wait — #19779 sat on `blocked` nearly two minutes longer than #19776) → confirm `added_to_merge_queue` → landing is `origin/main` with **parent count 1**. `pm:dispatched` is stripped by hand afterwards; it has survived the close on 9 of the last 9.
